_comment: Which voice speaks each line of the dialogues in data.js, and how each TTS
backend is asked for it. Words are NOT synthesised — they are native Lingua
Libre recordings or nothing, and tools/build_audio.py still owns them. This
file covers sentences only, which no single-word recording can ever supply.
A dialogue names its characters in `sp`, so each character gets its own
voice and a conversation sounds like two people rather than one reading a
script. The monologues carry no `sp`; `texts` assigns them a narrator.
Voice fields:
gender        male | female — the only attribute both backends understand.
instruct      OmniVoice voice-design string, overriding the one built from
`gender` + `dialect`. See docs/voice-design.md upstream.
ref/ref_text  Switch OmniVoice to voice cloning instead: a 3-10 second
reference clip and its transcript. NOTE the Lingua Libre
recordings are single words (~0.7 s) and are far too short
to clone from — a reference has to be built from connected
speech, and cloning a named contributor's voice to make them
say words they never recorded is a decision to take
deliberately, not a default. Hence: empty here.
leva_speaker  Built-in speaker name for the leva-tts backend. Run
`synth_lines.py --backend leva --list-voices` to print the
names the checkpoint actually ships; guessing them silently
falls back to the model's default speaker for every line,
which is exactly the one-voice-reads-the-script failure the
per-character mapping exists to avoid.
_speed: Under 1.0 because these are A1 listening texts. Slow enough to follow, not
so slow that the prosody stops sounding like speech — the old browser-TTS
_texts: Narrator for the texts that are monologues rather than dialogues. Naming
them here rather than defaulting keeps the two from sounding like the same
